"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The U.S. and Israel are planning another attack on Iran after the midterm elections.
It's according to an official not authorized to speak publicly.
NPR's Daniel Estrin has more.
All of this has been coming out just in the last few days.
On Sunday, President Trump endorsed Netanyahu for re-election.
Israelis go to the polls this coming Tuesday.
And Trump said the reason that he was endorsing him was that he said, "We may have to finish
the job in Iran," and that he would need Netanyahu and Israel's support to do that.
And ever since Trump endorsed Netanyahu, Netanyahu's been campaigning for re-election with the
promise that he will strike Iran.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reporting, "Connecticut Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal announced
an inquiry today into how SpaceX's star shield was slowed down for Ukraine's defense systems
exposing the country to Russian missile attacks.
It comes after the Trump administration has been providing mixed messages about what led
to the sudden restrictions, which came after President Trump threatened to withhold intelligence
from Ukraine and eased sanctions on Russia.
Today, Trump said the service is once again working at optimal speeds for Ukraine.
President Trump must answer questions under oath by December 11 for his $10 billion lawsuit
against the BBC or risk having it dismissed.
Trump sued in Florida, but the October 2024 BBC documentary that sparked the case was
never broadcast or streamed there, and appears David Falkenflick reports.
The British broadcasting giant apologized for splicing two bits of Trump's speech on
January 6, 2021, together.
The documentary made it seem he had made a direct call for violence to stop the formal
certification of the election won by Joe Biden just two months earlier.
The BBC's legal team now seeks to learn precisely what Trump thought he was doing with the speech.
After all, more than 200 January 6 defendants claimed in court that Trump had urged them
to siege Congress, quote, show strength and fight like hell.
Trump pulled out of a deposition scheduled for last Friday, citing matters of national
importance.
Trump spent the day campaigning for a Senate candidate in Georgia and out of GOP event
in Mar-a-Lago, his Florida resort, David Falkenflick and PR News, Miami.
With the midterm elections less than two weeks away, the Trump administration is announcing
billions of dollars in aid to farmers.
And PR's Kirk Sigler reports President Trump's tariffs and Iran war have strained global
fertilizer and diesel supplies.
The administration is spending a billion dollars to help fund the construction of eight domestic
fertilizer manufacturing plants from Florida to Iowa to California.
As follows, the president announcing at a campaign rally in Kansas this week the creation
of the new Harvest Fuel Relief Program, providing our farmers with $8 billion in support to
offset diesel costs during this harvest season.
With diesel prices at record highs, the president has been campaigning for Republicans lately
in rural red heartland states, where the GOP is now seen as vulnerable in November.
Kirk Sigler, NPR News.
Major U.S. stock indexes fell today.
This is NPR News.
U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche announced charges of drug trafficking and money laundering
against a powerful Democratic Virginia state senator, accusing her of leading a criminal
marijuana enterprise and using her office to enrich herself.
Senator Elle Louise Lucas has been a critic of President Trump and has characterized the
search as an attempt to intimidate her.
Crows have small brains, but new research finds they make quick, accurate decisions,
and PR's Ping Huang reports on the advantages of bird brains.
Kerry and Crows can take in visual information and make decisions about twice as fast as
humans and primates.
Andreas Neder is a comparative neuroscientist at the University of Tübingen in Germany.
For a long time, birds have been considered to be dumb creatures, which is totally wrong.
Birds are really fascinating, and you see many instances that evolution really pushed
them to the limit.
Neder and his colleagues gave Crows a common decision-making test, also used in humans
and primates.
He said the fact that Crows did it faster shows an advantage to how bird brains are organized.
Since they're more densely packed than monkey and human brains, signals don't travel
as far, so birds can process information more quickly.
The paper is published in the journal Science.
Ping Huang, NPR News.
Tourists and locals gathered at a temple in southern Egypt today to witness a rare solar
phenomenon.
Twice a year, for about 20 minutes, the sun illuminates the statues of Ramses II and two
gods inside the great temple of Ramses II.
This event marks the pharaoh's ascension and birthday.
I'm Rylan Barton from Washington.
This is NPR News.
